title: IC Substrate Inspection - Film Non-Uniformity Detection on 2920 Series
subtitle: Post-Oxidation Quality Validation for 10nm Node Manufacturing
author: Dr. Wei Zhang

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the 2920 Series system to detect and classify Film Non-Uniformity defects during post-oxidation inspection at the 10nm technology node. The test is conducted at Milpitas Fab B to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 450mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Film Non-Uniformity defects that are critical to yield at the 10nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the 2920 Series platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: 2920 Series
- Inspection Type: IC Substrate Inspection
- Target Defect: Film Non-Uniformity
- Process Step: Post-Oxidation
- Wafer Size: 450mm
- Technology Node: 10nm
- Fab Location: Milpitas Fab B

This test case applies to all 2920 Series systems deployed at Milpitas Fab B for post-oxidation monitoring in the 10nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: 2920 Series
Software Version: v15.0.308
Recipe: IC_SUBSTRATE_INSPECTION_10nm_POST_OXIDATION
Illumination Mode: Brightfield
Scan Speed: Medium (129 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 1.0μm
Edge Exclusion: 2mm
Sampling Plan: Full wafer sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the 2920 Series system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'IC Substrate Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Film Non-Uniformity defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 10nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 79 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 95% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±0.7% for IC Substrate Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.92 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2025-04-09
Wafers Tested: 47
Total Defects Found: 1724
Defect Density: 548.77 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 5.3%
Capture Rate: 99.3%
Test Duration: 99 minutes
System Uptime: 98.1%

Result Classification: CONDITIONAL PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The 2920 Series demonstrated acceptable performance in detecting Film Non-Uniformity at the 10nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate exceeds the target threshold; recipe tuning is recommended.

d) Minor calibration drift was detected after extended run; re-calibration resolved the issue.

e) The defect review station correlation was within specification.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Review edge-zone detection parameters for optimization.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Monitor performance over next 30 production days.
